EIML 2 · ICML 2026

Epistemic Intelligence in Machine Learning

10 July 2026 · Seoul, South Korea

This page preserves the published record of EIML 2 · ICML 2026. Dates, affiliations, and submission information refer to that edition.

Original workshop website · Current edition

Overview Topics Speakers Programme Papers Dates Committees Sources

About this edition

Reliable learning systems need to recognise when their knowledge is insufficient. The second workshop explored this ability, called epistemic intelligence, across problems such as distribution shift, hallucination, safety, and alignment.

Building on the first EIML workshop at EurIPS 2025, the programme connected foundational work on uncertainty with practical questions about how models can identify gaps in their knowledge, seek information, revise beliefs, and decide when to abstain.

Topics

Foundations of uncertainty
  • Representing incomplete knowledge through extensions of probability, including sets of distributions and higher-order models.
  • Distinguishing randomness, ambiguity, and ignorance, and studying rational learning and decisions under incomplete information.
  • Understanding the consequences for generalisation, model comparison, and robustness.
Uncertainty-aware generative AI and foundation models
  • Recognising uncertainty and mitigating hallucination in generative models.
  • Using uncertainty in decoding, prompting, inference, and reward modelling.
AI safety as an epistemic problem
  • Reasoning about failures that were not anticipated during development.
  • Identifying gaps in knowledge and supporting abstention, refusal, or safe fallback behaviour.
AI alignment under objective uncertainty
  • Learning when human objectives and preferences are incomplete, changing, or manipulated.
  • Representing uncertainty about values and examining the limits of preference learning.
Lifelong and continual learning in open worlds
  • Revising beliefs as conditions change and new concepts emerge.
  • Accumulating knowledge while retaining appropriate uncertainty and reducing catastrophic forgetting.

Call for papers

Submission information from the original call, retained for reference.

The workshop welcomed original research and work in progress on reasoning and decision-making under incomplete knowledge, including theoretical work, applications, benchmarks, and foundational perspectives.

Papers were submitted through OpenReview using the EIML 2026 LaTeX style. The call specified 4–6 pages, excluding references and supplementary material, with anonymised submissions for double-blind review.

The workshop was non-archival. Work previously shared in non-archival venues, or under review elsewhere, was eligible; authors were asked to check the policies of any other venue.

The call permitted language models as general-purpose writing assistants. It encouraged at least one author of each submission to volunteer as a reviewer.

The event was primarily in person, with authors asked to present posters where possible. The accepted-paper page subsequently specified eight-minute oral presentations and five-minute spotlights, each accompanied by a poster.

Notes on the historical record

This record preserves the published website as retrieved on 13 October 2026; affiliations reflect that source.

The Important Dates page updates author notification to 17 May 2026, while the homepage still says 15 May. The archive follows the explicit update on the Important Dates page and records the discrepancy here.

The original call mentioned ten-minute spotlights, while the accepted-paper list specifies eight-minute oral presentations and five-minute spotlights. The published programme is retained as its own record.

Fazl Barez’s talk title was published, but its abstract was still marked TBD when retrieved.

The programme committee entry “Buelte” is reproduced as listed; the source does not provide a given name.

Some original portraits and the sponsor image could not be retrieved. Names and affiliations are preserved, but no sponsor identity has been inferred from an inaccessible image.
